question: Which of the fruits shown in the 2008 painting "Embroidery from Uzbekistan" were served as part of the October 1949 breakfast menu for the ocean liner that was later used as a floating prop for the film "The Last Voyage"? Give the items as a comma-separated list, ordering them in clockwise order based on their arrangement in the painting starting from the 12 o'clock position. Use the plural form of each fruit.

history.name: MultiModalData_Expert
history.content: Plan: 1) Locate the 2008 painting "Embroidery from Uzbekistan" and identify depicted fruits with their positions (12 o'clock, clockwise). 2) Confirm which ocean liner was used as a floating prop in the film "The Last Voyage" (1960). 3) Find the SS Île de France October 1949 breakfast menu and list fruits. 4) Intersect fruits from painting and menu. 5) Order matches clockwise from 12 o'clock and output in plural, comma-separated.

history.name: WebNavigation_Expert
history.content: Found a gallery page featuring the 2008 painting "Embroidery from Uzbekistan" (contemporary still life). The image shows a central platter with fruits: at ~12 o'clock a cluster of pears; around ~2–3 o'clock a small bunch of bananas; lower-left around ~7 o'clock a split pomegranate; near bottom a small bunch of grapes. Will capture clockwise order starting at 12: pears (top), bananas (right), grapes/pomegranate (lower/left).

history.name: DataVerification_Expert
history.content: Verifying menu authenticity and date: Image shows "SS Île de France" header and an October 1949 stamp, breakfast service. Fresh Fruit section explicitly lists "Bananas" and "Pears." All consistent.

history.name: MultiModalData_Expert
history.content: Intersection of painting fruits with October 1949 breakfast menu fruits: pears and bananas. Painting clockwise order starting from 12 o'clock: pears at 12; next clockwise around 2–3 o'clock are bananas. Therefore, ordered list should be: pears, bananas.

history.name: WebNavigation_Expert
history.content: Double-checking the painting orientation: The pears are clearly at the top center of the platter (12 o'clock), and the bananas are to the right (about 2–3 o'clock). Clockwise from 12 yields pears then bananas.

history.content: Confirming the breakfast menu list: Both "Bananas" and "Pears" appear under Fresh Fruit for the October 1949 menu scan. No "Grapes" listed as fresh fruit; pomegranate not listed.

history.content: Preliminary result constructed per instructions: pears, bananas.
